scope: Proposition I.1 (Weighted major decomposition) of the manuscript “Quasipolynomial Bounds for Arithmetic Progressions” (preprints/Quasipolynomial-Bounds-for-Arithmetic-Progressions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 159 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 481eaf7730dc4d58), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 179. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Use the data U, Ch, Wh, ch, yh, βh of Proposi- tion F.2, with rank at least R in Definition F.1, and assume Properties 1 and 2 of that proposition on the sampled boxes and the ambient domain U. Assume also the uniform symbol step-drop statement of Lemma B.1. For every fixed degree bound s there is an exponent Cs with the following uniform property. Prescribe an early budget p, sampling dimensions, chart widths, a fraction at least e−p of productive paths, and slow and denominator bounds at most ep. The output bounds are at most exp((2 + p)Cs ) before choosing the perturbation size, scale range, rank threshold, or parent side lengths. Choose those later parameters sufficiently in that order, as in Proposition F.2. Write Ah = (Ch)[h] for the ordinary degree-h homogeneous part of Ch, and put A = (Ah)h. Give u weight 1 and bh weight h. Let D(u, b) be any fixed scalar weighted homogeneous polynomial of degree 1 ≤ d ≤ s, with no bound on its coefficients. If, after fixing short axes on each productive path, the degree-d homogeneous part of D(ψ(t), β(ψ(t))) in all the retained parameter variables is slow plus rational of the prescribed bounds on at least the prescribed fraction of paths, then there exist rational graded spaces Kh ⊃ Wh of early height and polynomials S, R such that, for b ∈ L h Kh, D(u, b) = S(u/H, b − A(u)) + R(u, b). (I.1) The coefficients of S and a common denominator of R have early bounds; the numerators of R are unrestricted. The assertion is simultaneous for polynomially many scalar polynomials, by intersecting their spaces. Long-variable thresholds and slice costs also have early bounds.
